openingMessage: If you don't have time to do it right, when will you have time to do it over?
openingWhy: A rushed handover — 'she's bled down, you're good' — with one valve still holding pressure is how the night hand ends up wearing what the day hand skipped. The five minutes a real handover takes is the cheapest time in the oilfield.
leadershipThought: This industry rewards preparation, effort, and ownership — not excuses. You help power homes, hospitals, schools, and communities. Take pride in the standard you represent.

specialFocus.title: Focus Friday: This Week's Top Performers, and What They All Do the Same Way
specialFocus.why:
Ray, close your week with the names. It's been a strong one, and today the focus is the people who made it that way. Read every name out loud, say what it was for, and give the circle a second to react before you move on. Ten minutes.

Start with the intent: nobody on this list did anything special. They did the ordinary things all the way through, on every form, on every well. That's the whole point. If your name isn't up here, the list below shows exactly what gets it there next week.

★ TOP OF THE BOARD: clean on two different days
  • Nathan Contreras, Monday and Tuesday: clean both days, and on Tuesday the only tech in the company with nothing at all to fix. Two trailer inspections, two wells, every photo taken that day.
  • Michael Jobe, Monday and Wednesday: clean both days, and Monday's form was the only one that wrote down a real correction: the crew had no tag line, and Jobe had them get one.
  • Humberto Marquez-Salazar, Tuesday and Wednesday: trailer 606 fully covered two days running. Three inspections plus the readiness form each day, every photo taken that day.
  • Jerry Gonzales, Tuesday and Wednesday: both trailer inspections and a complete close-out Tuesday, then a readiness form Wednesday with pressure and hydro date on every charged bottle.
  • Dennis Easley and Allen White, Tuesday and Wednesday: H2S dailies with every bottle written out, pressure and hydro date, two days in a row.
✓ ALSO EARNED IT THIS WEEK
  • Tyrell Sanders and Kedrick McCarter, Monday: nothing to fix on their wells. Full close-outs, every photo on the day.
  • Hayden Haugh, Wednesday: two trailer inspections and the well, complete from top to bottom.
  • Jacob Hernandez, Tuesday: two inspections, the readiness form and a full Learn section on the well.
  • Trevor McKenzie, Alexander Clubb, Bryan Medlin and Jimmy Cooper, Wednesday: readiness forms with pressure and hydro date on every charged bottle.
  • Robert Henigan, Tuesday: answered "anything wrong or missing?" with a plain "No" when every other form left it blank.
From Matt Croom's nightly reviews of Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday forms. Thursday's review wasn't in when this was written.
THE WEEK IN NUMBERS
  • 64 jobs on the Exxon board Monday through Thursday. Thursday alone was 21, with three below-grade Davit Arm jobs. Today's board has 17 more.
  • Uniform: techs answering "No" to Canon FR coveralls went from 3 on Monday to 2 on Tuesday to 1 on Wednesday.
  • Trailer inspections: 23 of 23 filed Monday and Tuesday.
  • The clean list grew every day. Wednesday's was the longest of the week: ten names.
Ten minutes: intent (1) · top of the board (3) · also earned it (2) · what they do the same way (3) · send-off (1).
specialFocus.standardLabel: What the Top Performers Do the Same Way
standard: Today's photos, taken today. Every clean form this week had every photo dated the day of the job. An old photo proves nothing about today.
Every charged bottle gets two things: the pressure and the hydro date. A date with no pressure is half an entry.
Every trailer, every day: both inspections and the readiness form. It doesn't matter which tech on the trailer files which one, as long as all three are in.
Finish the Learn section in your own words. One sentence about this well beats a list copied from the last one.
Answer every question. "No" is an answer. A blank isn't.
Write down the correction you made. "Crew had no tag line, had them get one" is one line, and it's the best line on a form all week.
Still Working at Height week: six feet or more, 100% tied off, and your rescue is named before you climb.

scenarios.title: Your Name on Monday's List
scenarios.body: It's Friday afternoon, last well of the week, and the crew wants to roll. The close-out is open on your phone. The photos from this morning's trailer inspection are still in your camera roll, the Learn section is blank, and the readiness form asks if anything is wrong or missing. This is the exact minute that decided every name read out today. Take today's photos, write one true sentence about this well, answer the question, and send it before you leave location. Ray, ask the circle: what's the one box you're most likely to skip at the end of a Friday?
